claims.statement: With `DECK_EVENT_LOG` set, `fileEventLog` creates the parent directory and appends one JSON line per event (`t` in epoch ms plus the event's own fields), swallowing write failures so logging can never affect the panel; when the variable is unset it returns null and nothing is recorded.

One `DECK_EVENT_LOG` value covers the whole process tree: the guard writes carry and single-instance events and spawns the panel with `env: process.env`, the panel writes boot/autostart/dataplane/usage/pin/quit events, and the renderer's `notify` records arrive through `deck:host-notify` — all interleaved in the same JSONL file, so the log must be read in timestamp order.

The whole process tree shares one console stream — the guard spawns the panel with `stdio: 'inherit'` and the data-plane child is forked the same way — which is where config warnings, icon-hide failures, autostart and migration failures, and the per-service `deck-*` / `agent-sessions:` warnings surface with no environment variable set at all.

On any data-plane child exit the host drops the child reference, rejects every pending RPC with `数据面子进程退出，请求失败`, logs `dataplane-exit {code}` and respawns after `min(30 s, 1 s · 2^attempt)`; any `ready` or `snapshot` message resets the attempt counter, and there is no in-process fallback collection path.

Degraded data-plane reads are asymmetric: before the first snapshot the port answers with placeholders (locally synthesized clock, empty sessions, zeroed gauges with `-- GB/-- GB`, empty desktop plan), while after a crash `latest` is never cleared so reads return the last snapshot — a frozen panel is therefore a stopped push, not a failing read.

`bootPanel` awaits `kernel.panelData.whenReady` before creating the window; it resolves on the child's first `ready` or `snapshot` message or after `DEFAULT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` (logging `dataplane-ready-timeout {timeoutMs}`), it is one-shot rather than a re-arming guard, and on timeout the panel opens on an empty data plane instead of not opening.

Data-plane write RPCs are exactly `desktop/move` and `desktop/reset-layout`; both reject with `数据面子进程不在场` when no child is present and with `数据面子进程退出，请求失败` when the child exits mid-request, whereas a business refusal (an item outside the scanned pool, a pinned dock item, an anchor in another zone) resolves in-band with `{ ok: false, error }`.

The data-plane child is forked with `serviceName: 'deck-dataplane'` and `stdio: 'inherit'`, so it is identifiable in a process listing and its collection warnings reach the panel's console; recorded `dataplane-spawn` events carry no `pid` because the child pid is still undefined when the line is written.

`collectSessions` isolates each tool scanner: a scanner that throws is skipped with the warning `agent-sessions: <tool> 扫描失败，跳过` while the remaining tools still render, and a whole-round failure in `SessionsService.refresh` empties the list (`deck-sessions: 本轮扫描失败，给空表`) rather than caching stale rows.

`DesktopService.refresh` catches a throwing scan round and keeps the previous round's item pool, logging `deck-desktop: 本轮扫描失败，沿用上一轮条目` — a deliberate contrast with the sessions service, which empties its list instead of serving stale state.

The weather card is the only front-end card that fetches on its own (Open-Meteo with coordinates from the snapshot, a 10-minute refresh and a 10 s abort); a failed fetch makes it print `FETCH FAILED` until the next attempt and emits the `weather-error` evidence record.

A session-row click never throws into the panel: `FocusService.focusTool` resolves to `focused` (an existing window brought forward), `launched` (no window and a configured exe) or `degraded` with a reason such as a missing `config.tools` entry or a refused foreground call, and the page records `session-focus-result` / `session-focus-failed`.

Search unavailability is classified at one point: a `ListaryNetworkError` from the loopback client and the `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` payload code both become `offline`, the kernel pushes `search/state offline` and re-sends the current query every 3 s while the overlay remains active, and the `ENGINE OFFLINE` badge is the renderer's reaction to that state (`search-offline-shown`).

An engine that is reachable but misbehaves (non-JSON body, unknown error code) is classified `error`, not offline: no badge is shown, no retry is scheduled, and the only trace is the console line `deck-search: 引擎响应异常，等下次输入`; the next input re-queries.

`config.search.port` (default 38431, validated as an integer in 1..65535 with a warning fallback, with the host fixed to the constant `127.0.0.1` and never read from configuration) is the only search knob and reaches the kernel at assembly time; pointing it at a dead port and restarting the panel is the accepted way to reproduce the engine-offline path, and it is exactly what the acceptance battery does.

The guard releases the icon claim through three paths — panel child exit (reason `panel-exit`, executed before `app.exit(code)`), a spawn failure (`panel-spawn-failed`) and its own `before-quit` (`outer-quit`) — using an idempotent `settled` flag and toggling only when this run hid the icons and they are still hidden.

The detached restore watcher is spawned by the guard only when `carry.didHide()` is true, runs as `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` with `detached` and ignored stdio, blocks in `WaitForSingleObject` on the guard's process object, and on wake calls `restoreIfHidden(null, 'guard-dead')` — a view-fact-only, silenced restore that always exits 0 and therefore leaves no evidence event of its own.

`electron . --icon-restore` is a one-shot self-rescue that runs before any single-instance logic (so it works while a panel is resident), logs `carry-boot {mode: 'restore'}`, calls `forceShowIcons` — which toggles only when the registry `HideIcons` preference is `1` — and exits with code 0.

A hidden-icon state left behind by a dead carry episode is indistinguishable from the user's own `HideIcons=1` preference, so the next guard run logs `icons-already-hidden`, records no hide obligation, and its later `icons-restored` performs no toggle at all — meaning the event name is not proof of visibility and only `prefHiddenAfter` / `viewVisibleAfter` reveal the resulting state.

The Startup entry `AGENT DECK.lnk` aims at `process.execPath` with the app directory as its single quoted argument and no mode flag (so a Startup boot runs the guard); it is created or healed only by a run whose application directory matches the declared `config.autostart.appDir`, a live link pointing elsewhere is kept, and `config.autostart.enabled = false` removes the link on every boot regardless of production identity.

Every boot that resolves the Startup path ends with one `autostart-applied {link, action, reason, applied}` record where `applied` is false for a failed write; a shortcut read failure logs `autostart-read-failed` and is then treated as an absent link (so a production run rewrites it), and legacy watchdog links are removed unconditionally and logged as `autostart-legacy-removed {names}`.

Before collection starts, `migrateUsageLog` copies the legacy day files from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qoder-deck\usage` into `userData/usage`, skipping non-day files and files outside the 90-day retention, accounting for progress per file in `.legacy-migrated.json`, and merging same-day content line-by-line so a rerun cannot double-count; a missing legacy directory is recorded as no history instead of being rescanned every boot.

A usage-log file that fails to migrate is deliberately not recorded, so that run writes no marker and logs `usage-migrate-failed {file, message}` for retry on the next boot; a completed pass logs `usage-migrated {migrated, failed, skipped}`, and because `bootPanel` wraps the whole call in try/catch a migration failure only degrades to history accumulating from zero and never blocks boot.

The dock's recommendation order is scored from `start-*.jsonl` with a 14-day half-life over a 90-day retention, which is why a partly migrated usage history presents as a flattened recommendation order rather than as a missing card.

All recall paths converge on `showPanel(reason)`, which shows the window inactive when it is minimized or hidden, re-pins it to the bottom and records `panel-shown` plus a `pin` line when that re-pin succeeds; the tray left click uses reason `tray-click` and a second launch uses `second-instance`.

Recall never raises the panel above ordinary windows: `pinToBottom` forces `HWND_BOTTOM` and the codebase makes no always-on-top call, so a panel that is merely covered by a maximized window stays covered even after a tray click or a second launch.

A second `electron .` launch is refused within milliseconds — the refused process logs `single-instance-refused {pid}` and exits 0 — while the running panel, which holds the single-instance lock for its whole life, receives Electron's `second-instance` event and recalls itself; a recorded run shows `pin {reason: 'show-second-instance'}`, `panel-shown {reason: 'second-instance'}` and then `single-instance-refused`.

The panel page is served from `dist/renderer` over the `deck-plugin://` protocol and the renderer declares its hotzones unconditionally when its module executes, so a window with no `hotzones` line after `boot` proves the renderer never ran (missing or stale build, protocol or script failure) rather than a data-plane problem.
